slides.texte_overlay:
learning a dead language

learn twenty words of latin or ancient greek. you'll start seeing their roots in half the words you use, and english suddenly makes so much more sense than before.

reading the footnotes

read the footnotes and sources in the next non fiction book you pick up. that's where the real arguments hide, and most readers skip right past them without a second look.

a daily lesson

spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in something new: astronomy, art history, economics. small doses every day build a mind that connects ideas without effort.
slides.texte_sophia:
a daily lesson

i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in something new: astronomy, art history, economics. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and my mind connects ideas easily now.

slides.texte_overlay:
solving riddles

solve one logic riddle a day with your morning coffee. puzzles train you to question your first answer, which is the core habit of every sharp thinker.

visiting small museums

visit small local museums instead of only the famous ones. fewer crowds, more time with each piece, and strange local stories you'd never hear anywhere else.
